overview: This Senate resolution mourns the death of Ben Nighthorse Campbell, a former U.S. senator and representative from Colorado, and honors his life. It describes his Air Force service during the Korean War, his place on the 1964 U.S. Olympic judo team as its first Native American member, and his career as a jewelry maker and rancher. It highlights his work in Congress, including writing the law that created the National Museum of the American Indian and serving as the only American Indian to chair the Senate Committee on Indian Affairs. The resolution sends word to the House and his family and has the Senate recess that day in his memory. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on January 15, 2026.
for: Supporters say honoring a former member who served his country in uniform and in both chambers of Congress is a long-standing and appropriate tradition.
against: Critics say it is symbolic and doesn't change any law or spending.
